intent.outcome: After this ships, mp milestone unblock <id> clears the block overlay on a milestone at any lifecycle value — terminal (complete or cancelled) and non-terminal — without regressing execution_status. A lifecycle=complete + execution_status=done + blocked=true milestone (the M159 debt pattern) stays at execution_status=done after unblock; an in-progress blocked milestone falls back to planned (the original behavior). The blocked, block_reason, blocked_at, blocked_by, deferred, cancelled overlay fields are cleared in both branches.

problem.description: crates/mp/src/milestone/complete.rs:210 unblock_milestone blindly sets m.milestone.execution_status = "planned".to_string() regardless of lifecycle. For a milestone at lifecycle=complete + spec_status=verified + execution_status=done (the terminal state after M158/M145 ceremony), blocking it externally via mp milestone block and then unblocking via mp milestone unblock regresses execution_status to planned. The terminal lifecycle is unchanged but the ceremony state is now inconsistent — mp show milestone --summary reports execution_status=planned for a lifecycle=complete milestone, which reads as unfinished. The single-session workaround used at the M159 close (commit d939a72 — mp milestone set-status 159 done after unblock) restored the field but is a footgun: a future operator who runs just mp milestone unblock lands in the same inconsistent state. There is no test guarding the regression today.

in_scope: Patch crates/mp/src/milestone/complete.rs:210-228 unblock_milestone to branch on m.milestone.is_terminal(). Non-terminal milestones continue to take execution_status = planned (the prior behavior). Terminal milestones (complete or cancelled) keep execution_status intact.

Audit crates/mp/src/milestone/complete.rs for other primitives that may regress terminal lifecycle the same way (defer_milestone, reopen_milestone) and triage; the fix lands on unblock_milestone in M166, follow-ups for the others if the audit finds matches.

Add integration tests under crates/mp/tests/unblock_milestone_preserves_terminal.rs: (a) complete + blocked to unblock to execution_status='done' (the M159 pattern); (b) in-progress + blocked to unblock to execution_status='planned' (regression-pin the prior behavior); (c) cancelled + blocked to unblock to execution_status='cancelled'; (d) unblock on a non-blocked milestone continues to refuse with the existing bail.
Document the branch in the inline doc-comment on unblock_milestone (crates/mp/src/milestone/complete.rs) and link to the M159 precedent in mp-dogfood-log.md entry 26 (post-ship).
out_of_scope: Touching `set_execution_status` or `set_status` surface — `set_execution_status` (crates/mp/src/milestone/complete.rs:18) regresses terminal milestones on the `blocked`/`planned`/`deferred` arms: the lifecycle-update match at complete.rs:88-108 only fires for `in-progress` and `done`; the other status values overwrite execution_status while leaving lifecycle unchanged. Real-world reach is narrow (the natural block+unblock workflow goes through block_milestone/unblock_milestone, not set_execution_status, and M166 patched those), but the regression is reproducible via `mp milestone set-status <id> blocked ; set-status <id> planned` on a complete milestone. Logged for a follow-up — out of M166 scope.

Rewriting block_milestone — the bug is on unblock, not block; block correctly sets execution_status=blocked + blocked=true regardless of terminal value (a terminal milestone can be blocked for cosmetic / debt-tracking reasons; that's not the subject of M166).
Adopting a unified effective_execution_status everywhere — the field is stable enough to leave direct, and that work belongs in a state-machine refactor, not a 5-line patch.
Audit of execution_status writes outside the milestone crate — out of scope; the field is the source of truth.

design_decisions.choice: Branch on m.is_terminal() (a MilestoneFile helper at crates/mp-model/src/milestone.rs:1334 — impl MilestoneFile, line 1334); terminal milestones keep their on-disk execution_status value unchanged rather than being forced to done or cancelled.
design_decisions.rationale: is_terminal() already encodes the right predicate (lifecycle in {complete} || cancelled=true) and is used by other gate checks in the codebase. Forcing a done write would erase the audit signal of how the milestone arrived at the terminal state. Preserving-on-terminal is conservative: if M159's on-disk execution_status=blocked was set by an external block-while-terminal, unblock restores the prior value.

design_decisions.choice: Triage defer_milestone and reopen_milestone for the same regression pattern but land the fix only on unblock_milestone in M166. Open follow-ups for the others if the audit finds matches.
design_decisions.rationale: The bug surfaced via the M165 → M159 unblock path. Other primitives may carry the same flaw, but YAGNI on speculative refactor. The audit task (in_scope) lists the regressions; the remediation lands per-primer in follow-up milestones once confirmed.

findings.description: The M166 sibling audit (recorded in the commit message) notes that defer_milestone at crates/mp/src/milestone/complete.rs:247 unconditionally sets execution_status='deferred'. A terminal milestone (lifecycle=complete or cancelled=true) defer-then-undefer cycle would regress execution_status to the wrong value, mirroring M166's bug shape. Worth a follow-up milestone if real-world defer-then-undefer patterns on terminal milestones are observed; for now logged as documentation. The patch in M166 is intentionally narrow — defer_milestone is out of scope per the in_scope/out_of_scope split.
findings.author: ext-reviewer
findings.summary: defer_milestone carries the same regression shape — sibling primitive audit

findings.description: The M166 patch changed the cancelled-clear behavior so a cancelled milestone retains execution_status='cancelled' through block+unblock instead of having it erase the cancellation. But unblock_milestone still resets m.cancelled=false in the same write, so the only on-disk signal for the cancellation is the execution_status value. Downstream readers that check m.cancelled for the cancelled flag (vs checking execution_status) now diverge. M166's resolution is correct but introduces a magic-string coupling that a future M-NNN could clean up by either: (a) restoring the m.cancelled=true preservation in unblock_milestone for already-cancelled milestones; or (b) splitting the cancelled signal into its own field (separate from the execution_status string). Either way is a separate refactor. Honorable as M166 is incomplete cleanup; the test 'cancelled_blocked_unblock_keeps_cancelled' pins both invariants today.
findings.author: ext-reviewer
findings.summary: execution_status='cancelled' is now load-bearing after M166 — magic-string coupling risk

findings.description: The M166 patch fixes block_milestone + unblock_milestone (crates/mp/src/milestone/complete.rs:191, 221) to branch on is_terminal(), but the regression is still reachable via mp milestone set-status <id> blocked followed by mp milestone set-status <id> planned because set_execution_status (the backing mutator at crates/mp/src/milestone/complete.rs:18) has no is_terminal() guard. Concrete repro against this repo's own plan (using target/release/mp built from 591d3c9): stamp a milestone to lifecycle=complete + spec_status=verified + execution_status=done (the M159 stack), then run 'mp milestone set-status 01 blocked' — execution_status becomes 'blocked', blocked=true, lifecycle unchanged at 'complete'; then run 'mp milestone set-status 01 planned' — execution_status becomes 'planned', blocked=false, lifecycle still 'complete'. Final on-disk state: lifecycle='complete' + execution_status='planned' + blocked=false — the M159 regression shape, byte-identical to the pre-M166 block+unblock bug. mp validate --summary reports 0 errors / 0 warnings on this state (W-LC-TERMINAL only fires on lifecycle='done', not 'complete'); mp show milestone --summary reports execution_status='planned' on a complete milestone. The spec's out_of_scope claim at master-plan/milestones/166-...json:42 ('set_execution_status or set_status surface — those are already correct') is incorrect: set_execution_status only updates lifecycle on the 'in-progress' and 'done' arms (complete.rs:89-108); for 'blocked'/'planned'/'deferred'/'cancelled' it overwrites execution_status while leaving lifecycle unchanged. Fix: add an is_terminal() guard at the top of the with_milestone_mut_unlocked closure in set_execution_status that bails (or no-ops the execution_status write) when m.is_terminal() and status is one of the overlay / non-terminal-promotion values. Pin with a new test analogous to complete_plus_blocked_unblock_keeps_done but driving the regression through set-status. Also consider widening W-LC-TERMINAL in crates/mp/src/validate/plan.rs:626-649 to fire on lifecycle='complete' + execution_status not in {done,cancelled}, so the silent regression surface is at least surfaced even if set_execution_status stays unpatched. Same shape applies to defer_milestone (F-01) and any future non-lifecycle-following setter.
findings.author: ext-reviewer-2nd-pass
findings.summary: M159 regression still reachable via mp milestone set-status — set_execution_status has no is_terminal guard

findings.description: crates/mp/tests/unblock_milestone_preserves_terminal.rs:266-272 (the docstring block above the cancelled==true assertion in cancelled_blocked_unblock_keeps_cancelled) describes pre-M166 behavior: 'The cancelled overlay is cleared by unblock (M100 ER-1 paranoia clear) — this is symmetric with the deferred-clear; the execution_status stays terminal because of the M166 fix. The net effect on disk: blocked=false, cancelled=false, execution_status='cancelled'.' The 'cancelled=false' wording describes the old (pre-M166) paranoia-clear at complete.rs:223 that M166 explicitly removes (see complete.rs:256-262 — 'M166: do NOT clear cancelled here. ... wiping the overlay on unblock would erase the cancellation.'). The assertion on line 273 (assert_eq!(after_unblock['milestone']['cancelled'], true)) is the post-M166 behavior and is correct, but the preceding comment contradicts it. Fix: rewrite the comment to describe post-M166 behavior, e.g. 'M166 explicitly removes the prior paranoia-clear of cancelled; the overlay survives unblock along with execution_status='cancelled'. The net effect on disk: blocked=false, cancelled=true, execution_status='cancelled'. This is the contract F-02 flagged — the cancelled signal is now load-bearing through the magic string in execution_status.'

findings.summary: Stale comment in test 3 describes pre-M166 paranoia-clear that M166 explicitly removes

findings.description: M166 spec at master-plan/milestones/166-...json:36, 81, 103 describes the new guard as 'branch on m.milestone.is_terminal() (a MilestoneMeta helper at crates/mp-model/src/milestone.rs:1334)'. The implementation at crates/mp/src/milestone/complete.rs:207 and 242 calls m.is_terminal() — and the helper is defined on MilestoneFile (impl MilestoneFile, crates/mp-model/src/milestone.rs:1334), not on MilestoneMeta. There is no MilestoneMeta::is_terminal in the codebase. This is a minor doc inaccuracy — the behaviour is correct, but a future reader chasing the cited site will look in the wrong struct. Fix: change 'm.milestone.is_terminal() (a MilestoneMeta helper)' to 'm.is_terminal() (a MilestoneFile helper)' in the in_scope bullet (line 36), design_decisions choice (line 81), and S1 action (line 103). Optionally add an M-numbered reference to the LIFECYCLE_TERMINAL constant at crates/mp-model/src/milestone.rs:58 for context.

findings.description: M166 spec out_of_scope bullet at master-plan/milestones/166-...json:42-46 reads: 'Touching set_execution_status or set_status surface — those are already correct (crates/mp/src/milestone/spec.rs:362 + MilestoneMeta::set_execution_status keep execution_status and lifecycle consistent at all literal values).' Two problems: (a) the cited site crates/mp/src/milestone/spec.rs:362 is a closing brace on a struct literal (no functional code there — verified by reading the file); (b) there is no MilestoneMeta::set_execution_status in crates/mp-model/src/milestone.rs (verified by grep). Both citations point to nothing. More substantively, the claim that set_execution_status 'keep[s] execution_status and lifecycle consistent at all literal values' is FALSE: the implementation at crates/mp/src/milestone/complete.rs:18-110 only updates m.milestone.lifecycle on the 'in-progress' (line 90) and 'done' (line 105) arms. For status='blocked'|'planned'|'deferred'|'cancelled', the function overwrites execution_status while leaving lifecycle unchanged — a real inconsistency on terminal milestones (see F-03 for the regression repro). Fix: replace the out_of_scope bullet with a more honest framing that names the actual risk ('set_execution_status regresses terminal milestones on the overlay / planned arms; deferred to a follow-up because the regression is only reachable via mp milestone set-status, not via the natural block+unblock workflow'), drop the nonexistent code references, and link to F-03.
findings.author: ext-reviewer-2nd-pass
findings.summary: Spec out_of_scope justification for set_execution_status cites nonexistent code and a false claim

findings.description: crates/mp/tests/unblock_milestone_preserves_terminal.rs:281-296 (unblock_milestone_refuses_non_blocked) calls unblock on the minimal-ready fixture (01-foundation.json), which starts at execution_status='done' + blocked=false. Both the pre-M166 bail (execution_status != 'blocked') and the post-M166 bail (!m.milestone.blocked) fire 'milestone is not blocked' for this fixture — the test passes either way and does not pin the M166 refactor that swaps the bail source from execution_status to the blocked overlay. The spec at master-plan/milestones/166-...json:72-73 claims AC-04 pins 'the existing bail on unblock_milestone for a non-blocked milestone continues to refuse with the same error message' — that contract is met, but the underlying mechanism change (overlay is now source of truth) is not exercised. Concrete fixture that would distinguish the two paths: a milestone with execution_status='blocked' but blocked=false (a legacy pre-M166 inconsistency that survives the bulk lifecycle migration). Pre-M166: bail does not fire, unblock proceeds and slams execution_status='planned' (the prior bug). Post-M166: bail fires with 'milestone is not blocked' (the new contract). Fix: add a second test variant (e.g., unblock_milestone_refuses_legacy_execution_status_blocked_with_overlay_false) that constructs the legacy inconsistency and asserts the bail fires. Tag it as honoring the new contract rather than as a regression-pin of the old one.
findings.author: ext-reviewer-2nd-pass
findings.summary: Test 4 doesn't pin the bail-mechanism change; both pre- and post-M166 pass the chosen fixture

findings.description: Verified empirically: after reproducing the regression shape via set-status (F-03 repro: lifecycle='complete' + execution_status='planned' on a milestone whose spec_status='verified'), mp validate --summary reports {error_count: 0, warning_count: 0, ok: true}. W-LC-TERMINAL at crates/mp/src/validate/plan.rs:626-649 only fires when lifecycle='done' (the executor-finished, awaiting-review state), not when lifecycle='complete' (the terminal state) — so the M159 regression shape (lifecycle=complete + execution_status regressed to a non-terminal value) is silent. This is a real gap because the M166 patch's whole premise is that this inconsistency is harmful — yet validate won't surface it when the patch is bypassed (via set-status, per F-03, or via future regressions on any other non-lifecycle-following setter). Fix: extend W-LC-TERMINAL to also fire when lifecycle='complete' and effective_execution_status(m) is not 'done' or 'cancelled' (the two terminal values). Mirror the existing skip-if-cancelled guard at line 627 so a cancelled milestone stays silent. Pair with an integration test in crates/mp/tests/validate_terminal_consistency.rs (or extend an existing validate suite) that asserts the warning fires on a synthesized complete+execution_status='planned' milestone.
findings.author: ext-reviewer-2nd-pass
findings.summary: mp validate does not catch lifecycle='complete' + execution_status not in {done, cancelled} — the M159 regression is silent
